text:
How was Wings on the air so long?
Wing was a kind of spin-off/knock off of Cheers. After the success of Cheers, David Angell, Peter Casey, and David Lee set out to create another different workplace comedy that would allow the core cast to primarily stay put in one set and have the stories evolve around the people that come and go, passing through the workplace. 
 Wings ran from 1990-1997 and 172 episodes. It was never a critical darning. The show received 3 Emmy nominations over its run, but one was for make-up and the other two were for guest appearances. It’s seemed to kind of rely on the cast of Cheers popping in time and again. The theme song, Frank Schubert’s Piano Sonata No. 20 in A Major is a far cry from any of the catchy theme songs of the 90’s. 
 The characters are pleasant. The comedy is harmless, but as a show it is, at best, background noise. I remember watching it during the original run when there was little or nothing else on. I’m watching it now and I just can’t figure out how it survived as long as it did. Was it inexpensive to make? Was is consistent enough to not mess with it. Were powerhouse shows like Cheers, Frasier, Seinfeld, and Friends carrying NBC enough that they just let it slide? I don’t know.
 Does anyone here have any insights as to why Wings ran so long?

text:
If you could choose to see a reunion, either as a stand alone film, mini series or series rebirth. Which of these shoes would you choose?

I'm specifically choosing series' here that it's known within the community and fanbase that these particular shows are ones that the fans and maybe even the cast have all talked about the desire to continue the story their creators have been telling.. anyone familiar with more than one show on this list provided here should see how they connect in that particular way.
 If you feel strongly about a show not listed, tell us what it is and why, but pls, try and choose from the list as well.
 The show I expect to have the least amount of casual fans who might know the show here, outside its own bubble would be. Venture brothers people who know this show know that it is very deep in world building and lore story telling. Unfortunately it was cancelled abruptly and was given just one film, which plays like a long episode to try and wrap up 7 seasons of world building, and while the finalé was fantastic. It fell short of being the perfect cap on the stories they had been unraveling for nearly 2 decades (that's right. 7 seasons took them nearly 20 years).
 If this was brought back, I would want to see it done in maybe a mini series and maybe another final film. But done with the knowledge that this is the end, that way the return would be building to something meaningful and on purpose.
 The next option would be community. Most of us know about community and their 6 seasons and a movie. Far as I know the final film is already written and it's just about finding the time to film it where everyone is available. I sure hope we get to see all the classics come back... Seeing troy come back will be amazing. I'm excited to see Nigel again, especially now that he's become so famous in recent years.... I personally hope we get to see the original cast interacting with the newer characters like paget Brewster and Keith David.
 Next we have arrested development. What can I say that most people don't already know. Clearly the story webe been following is all but finished. But I think it would be cool to see what happens next but with a story focused more on George Michael and maebe. Maybe something more like a back door pilot than a continuation of the original story and it's conclusion, which most of us find lackluster
 Burn notice is a show that ran for a long time but was never considered a real juggernaut when it came to ratings, even running on cable like tbs, so many people slept on this. But like arrested development, this show could find a new audience by bringing in a new, younger crew stuck somewhere and MacGyvering through episodes using their superpowers for good and trying to figure out who burned them.
 Can you think of a show that likely will never come back but probably could have success finding a new audience?
 It's worked for adventure time, Roseanne, full house, boy meets world and so so many more. But of course,for every successful one there a dozen failures

Sitcom characters that went on a downward spiral because (allegedly) their actors weren't getting along with the producers

These are the first two that came to mind. Charlie Sheen got addicted to drugs and became a pain in the ass to work with during his last couple seasons, eventually getting fired. And from what I've heard, some people who worked on the Office were upset at Ed Helms taking time off to go film the Hangover movies. 
 Both characters had their lives fall apart during the final seasons, also causing an infamous incident in their shows. With Charlie it was definitely when he threw up on a baby at the coffee shop, and with Andy I think it's either him taking a crap on David's car, or the "I can so just sit here and cry" scene. I feel like the changes in their characters were too drastic and negative to just be part of the planned storyline. IMO there's a good chance the writers/producers had ulterior motives, but who knows

text:
Moments where sitcoms got more bizarre due to running out of steam
Sorry if this was asked here before because a trope that suddenly stuck out to me was that trope where a sitcom doesn’t know what to do with its plots anymore as suddenly out of place elements start showing up out of nowhere.
Some examples of the trope being used are The Great Gazoo in the Flintstones and Steve Urkel’s crazy inventions in Family Matters as I started to notice how both shows were relatively grounded for the most part, but started in adding in sci fi elements that felt out of place.
Like when I look back at the aforementioned Great Gazoo subplot showing up in the Flintstones, I have to question why he was suddenly thrown in the show given how the show was a series set in the Stone Age, so I have no idea on why the writers threw in a character that would have been more suitable for a sci fi based show.
label: opinion
